titel: Voting for water and surviving a hurricane

faehigkeiten.grund: Dynamik weder belegt noch ausgeschlossen: keine Merkmale gefunden, aber eine unveraenderte Wiederholungsprobe beweist nichts

einzeiler: First-hand accounts of a historic water vote, a devastating hurricane and other…
kurzfassung: Max Pearson presents historical accounts including Uruguay's constitutional water referendum, the destruction caused by Hurricane Lewis in Antigua, a deadly plane hijacking in Karachi, a photo album exposing the normality of life at Auschwitz, and the origins of Northern Ireland's peace movement. The episode also explores the story of Ghanaian sprinting pioneer Alice Anum. Through personal testimonies, witnesses reflect on moments of tragedy, survival, and activism.
stichpunkte: Uruguay became the first country to enshrine water as a human right in its constitution following a 2004 referendum.
Hurricane Lewis struck Antigua in 1995, destroying homes and infrastructure while leaving lasting ecological damage.
Pan Am Flight 73 was hijacked by Palestinian militants in Karachi in 1986, resulting in a 16-hour ordeal and the deaths of 22 people.
A discovered WWII photo album revealed SS officers enjoying leisure time and celebrations while stationed at Auschwitz.
The tragic deaths of three children in a 1976 car crash sparked mass peace marches in Northern Ireland, leading to a Nobel Peace Prize for the movement's founders.
Ghanaian sprinter Alice Anum reflected on her Olympic career and becoming the original bearer of the Baby Jet nickname.

beschreibung:
Max Pearson presents a collection of the week's Witness History episodes.
We learn why, in 2004, Uruguayans voted to enshrine water as a human right in their constitution - the first country in the world to do so. And environmental historian Ellen Arnold reveals how water has shaped human history.
Also, we tell the story of the fatal hijacking of Pan Am Flight 73 in Pakistan, 40 years ago. And how the island of Antigua was devastated when Hurricane Luis hit the Caribbean in 1995.
We find out more about the abandoned Nazi photo album revealing the chilling normality of life at the Auschwitz concentration camp. Plus, how a Northern Ireland peace movement was born from one family’s tragedy.
Finally, in Sporting Witness, why Ghana’s sprinting superstar Alice Annum won the nickname ‘Baby Jet’.
Contributors:
Carmen Sosa - member of the water workers trade union.
Ellen Arnold – environmental historian.
Eli Fuller – Antigua resident.
Madhvi Bahunga - Pan-American Airways flight attendant.
Rebecca Erbelding – archivist and historian.
Gerry Grehan - chairperson of the Peace People.
Alice Annum - Ghanian sprinter.
